source_excerpts.text:
**Status: unvalidated physical-operation hypothesis. No experiment performed; no discovery of a new physical capability established. Historical novelty unresolved.**

## Proposed operation

Reorient the preferred chemical-order axis of immobilized FeNi domains by applying directional mechanical loading while a temporary nitrogen-rich phase forms; remove the load, extract nitrogen, and retain a different chemical-order-axis distribution in the final metal. The stronger test is to write one axis and then a different axis in the same immobilized material through another chemical cycle.

This is not a proposal simply to magnetize a metal. The proposed persistent output is a changed direction of the Fe/Ni layering, not only a changed spin direction. Nor is nitrogen insertion/topotactic extraction itself new. Epitaxial precursor-to-metal orientation transfer is also established prior work. Direct stress-assisted FeNi ordering has prior art. The narrower unresolved claim concerns chemical reorientation of fixed material without epitaxial templating or mechanical rotation of whole particles.

## What the investigation did

Screened metal purification, low-temperature ceramic forming, phonon control of ionic motion, and rare-earth-free magnetic materials. Examined primary publications, accessible supplementary diffraction figures and a calculated intensity table, and manufacturer magnetic specifications. Consulted Astra repository navigation and searched for tetrataenite/FeNi after opportunity selection; these targeted connector searches returned no matches, not a proof that the repository contains no related work.

No raw instrument data were acquired. The directly inspected supplementary table contains calculated powder intensities, not new or raw observations. Some full manuscripts were inaccessible. Container downloads failed; that failure is preserved in `sources/download_log.json`. Source URLs below permit later retrieval. No source PDF is bundled.

## Central missing interface

The unknown is a retained, stress-dependent chemical-axis response after nitrogen removal, in the same immobilized specimen and processing regime.

source_excerpts.text:
Let a domain have unit chemical axis n, nonnegative ordered volume dV, and order magnitude S. Define unnormalized tensors

    M = integral n n^T dV,       f = trace M,
    W = integral S^2 n n^T dV.

The requested volume-weighted tensor is Q=M/f when f>0. A normalized superlattice pole tensor is W/trace W only when its corrected/integrated intensity actually obeys this additive model. These are different targets. Coherent antiphase interference, incomplete angular/satellite integration, unknown structure factors, absorption, phase contamination and instrument normalization can invalidate the W acquisition interface. A theoretical tensor is not an acquired observable.

## Exact counterexample to the proposed simple contrast

Keep two fixed domain populations, each of volume 1/2, with axes x and y. In the first loading condition set Sx=4/5,Sy=2/5; in the second swap these magnitudes. Then

    M1=M2=diag(1/2,1/2,0),
    W1=diag(8/25,2/25,0), W2=diag(2/25,8/25,0).

Both total ordered volumes and total superlattice weights are unchanged. The normalized intensity contrast D_int=(Wxx-Wyy)/traceW changes from 3/5 to -3/5, a difference 6/5, with no axis reorientation at all. Persistence, repeatability and constant total intensity do not resolve this counterexample. An independently tracked degree of order for each orientation population would be additional information.

## Sharp identified set with an acquired order floor

Assume independently calibrated 0<s<1 and s<=S<=1 for every included domain, plus acquired total f. For a supplied W, the exact set of possible M over unrestricted unit-axis support is

    s^2 M <= W <= M,     trace M=f,       (Loewner order).

Necessity follows by integrating the positive rank-one matrices (S^2-s^2)nn^T and (1-S^2)nn^T. For sufficiency let

    P=(W-s^2 M)/(1-s^2),    R=(M-W)/(1-s^2).

Then P,R are PSD, M=P+R and W=P+s^2 R. Spectral decompositions of P and R realize the pair by finitely many domains at order magnitudes 1 and s, respectively. They need not commute. This establishes exact attainability, not only an outer bound. Feasibility requires traceW<=f<=traceW/s^2 and W PSD; those conditions also suffice by taking M proportional to W (zero case treated separately).

For known restricted axis support {n_i}, the exact finite-mixture model must instead retain M=sum m_i n_i n_i^T and W=sum w_i n_i n_i^T, with s^2 m_i<=w_i<=m_i,
